title: R' Yudan of Magdalaya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: [Taanit, chapter 1, halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Taanit.1.3.4), relates that Rabbi Yosi bar Yaakov went up to visit Rabbi Yudan of Magdalaya. While he was there, rain fell, and he heard a voice saying: “A thousand thousands—we are obliged to give thanks.” He asked, “Where did you get this?” He answered, “This is how Rabbi Simon, my teacher, blesses.” The same appears in Berakhot, chapter 9, at the end of halakhah 2. [Bereshit Rabbah 13:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.13.15) gives the name as Rabbi Yehudah of Magdalah.[^1]

notes.text: עד דהוה תמן means “while he was there.” קליה is his voice, not necessarily the sound of the rain. Hyman shortens the blessing with a dash. The second רבי after Simon means “my teacher.” The Berakhot abbreviation פ״ט סה״ב means chapter 9, end of halakhah 2. Bereshit Rabbah gives the variant Rabbi Yehudah of Magdalah where Taanit has Rabbi Yudan of Magdalaya.
